evidence.claim: Amnesty said the federal government restricted aid to Tigray, halted deliveries from August to November, held thousands of Tigrayan detainees arbitrarily, failed to implement accountability, and significantly eroded freedom of expression.
evidence.title: Amnesty International Report 2022/23; The State of the World's Human Rights; Ethiopia 2022
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the federal government restricted aid to Tigray, halted deliveries from August to November, held thousands of Tigrayan detainees arbitrarily, failed to implement accountability, and significantly eroded freedom of expression.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: ecoi.net is a secondary host, but the text is Amnesty’s country-report summary and is internally specific about 2022 conduct.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 with a concise year-end synthesis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is attributable to Abiy Ahmed’s federal government, though some conduct was implemented by security forces and regional actors.
contrary_evidence: The same source also notes the March humanitarian truce and partial resumption after the November agreement.
Some abuse was committed by Tigrayan forces in Afar, so not all violence is federal-side.

evidence.claim: The national dialogue excluded key rebel groups, and opposition figures accused the government of trying to orchestrate the process and control who participated.
evidence.title: Ethiopia launches a national dialogue, but divisions run deep
evidence.excerpt: The national dialogue excluded key rebel groups, and opposition figures accused the government of trying to orchestrate the process and control who participated.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Field reporting with named interlocutors, concrete dates, and direct quotations from critics and the commission.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022 with retrospective context from late 2021 on commission formation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The article attributes the process to Abiy's government and his public push for the dialogue, but also records that the commission claimed independence; attribution is mixed and not equivalent to a proven personal directive.
contrary_evidence: The commission and government argued the dialogue was inclusive and open to peaceful participants.
The report also notes some observers saw the process as potentially useful if managed properly.

evidence.claim: The National Dialogue Commission signed a partnership agreement with the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council to work in collaboration.
evidence.title: National Dialogue Commission, Civil Society Organizations Council Ink Partnership Agreement
evidence.excerpt: The National Dialogue Commission signed a partnership agreement with the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council to work in collaboration.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official contemporaneous report on a formal government-supported institutional step; credible for the existence of the agreement, less so for its effectiveness.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly about political-process institutions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects a state-backed institutional initiative under Abiy's government; it is strong for formal commitment, weaker for proving independent operation or actual openness.
contrary_evidence: The agreement does not show that the dialogue was truly independent or inclusive in practice.
Earlier and later reporting still described exclusion and control concerns.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said Article 93 allows suspension of political and democratic rights during a state of emergency, and that authorities used emergency powers in late 2021 and early 2022 to crack down on media houses and arrest online and broadcast journalists.
evidence.title: Ethiopia: Freedom on the Net 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said Article 93 allows suspension of political and democratic rights during a state of emergency, and that authorities used emergency powers in late 2021 and early 2022 to crack down on media houses and arrest online and broadcast journalists.
evidence.source_locator: country report text around Article 93 and the state-of-emergency discussion
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Established rights monitor with direct country-report analysis and specific legal-context claims.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to the 2022 period and the emergency powers still affecting the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to federal authorities under Abiy's government; the report separates legal basis from the implementation of restrictions, but not every action is individually ordered by him in the text.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes that the six-month state of emergency was lifted in February 2022, so some restrictions were inherited from the prior emergency period.

evidence.claim: Access Now said authorities had kept Tigray under an internet shutdown for two years, preventing communication, access to information, and accountability over violence.
evidence.title: Two years of internet shutdowns: people in Tigray, Ethiopia, deserve better
evidence.excerpt: Access Now said authorities had kept Tigray under an internet shutdown for two years, preventing communication, access to information, and accountability over violence.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs of the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous rights-monitor reporting on a specific shutdown and its political effects.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and explicitly about the shutdown's duration up to that date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Ethiopian authorities; this supports the de facto command path even though the underlying written order is not exposed in the public source.
contrary_evidence: Access Now is an advocacy source, so it is strong on the existence and effect of the shutdown but weaker on the precise internal command chain.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 nuclear, CBRN, cyber, AI, or equivalent catastrophic-risk decision by Abiy Ahmed.
No ruler-level command-and-control, safety, or custody evidence tied to a real nuclear posture.
No national election or transfer event occurred in 2022, so the core contestability and succession test is underdetermined.
No public 2022 command-chain document for shutdowns, accreditation revocations, or similar restrictions.
No traceable 2022 evidence of Abiy's own self-enrichment, hidden assets, or close-family benefit.
No public 2022 compliance trail for asset disclosure, conflicts of interest, or procurement/audit findings tied to Abiy.
No direct evidence tying the media crackdown or shutdowns to Abiy's personal benefit or concealment rather than state security policy.
